sections.label: The market landscape
paragraphs: I studied the Danish food delivery market and looked at competitors like HelloFresh and Too Good To Go. Talked to the founders, marketing team, and operations about what set them apart.

sections.label: The insight
paragraphs: Other companies were talking about sustainability. Eat Grim needed to celebrate it visually.

sections.label: Understanding the audience
paragraphs: I identified who actually cared. Eco-conscious consumers who wanted convenience, but also health and transparency. The messaging couldn't be guilt-based. It had to be something people wanted to be part of.

sections.label: Visual approach
paragraphs: The brand needed to be playful and bold. Colors that popped. A visual style that made wonky vegetables look exciting. Custom illustrations that felt hand-drawn and warm, not corporate.

sections.label: Unboxing experience
paragraphs: When someone got a box from Eat Grim, opening it should feel like an experience, not just receiving groceries.

sections.label: Creating consistency
paragraphs: The brand toolkit tied everything together: logo, typeface, color palette, and a recognizable 'wonky' fruit symbol. Consistency across everything meant people recognized Eat Grim instantly on Instagram, in their mailbox, or on a merchandise sticker.

sections.label: Packaging as storytelling
paragraphs: The brand identity came to life across dozens of touchpoints. The packaging for each box size was designed to spark curiosity with bold visuals, educational snippets, and a friendly tone that explained where the food came from and why it mattered.

sections.label: Visual content
paragraphs: Photography and illustration brought the mission to life. Every image showed the beauty in imperfect produce. Social media, newsletters, and campaigns were packed with vibrant images and behind-the-scenes stories.

sections.label: Digital presence
paragraphs: The website balanced storytelling with conversion, making it easy to sign up while telling the story of why it mattered.

sections.label: Extended brand presence
paragraphs: Merchandise extended the brand everywhere. Tote bags, t-shirts, posters, stickers, and email templates all carried the same playful energy. Over two years, the brand grew beyond a service into a movement people wanted to be part of.

sections.label: The growth
paragraphs: Eat Grim reached 2,500 regular subscribers during the two-year collaboration. More importantly, the brand sparked real conversations about food waste.

sections.label: Changing perception
paragraphs: The playful, punchy design made sustainability feel exciting instead of guilt-inducing. By using striking imagery, bold colors, and empowering messaging, the brand made people feel good about the choice they were making every week.

sections.label: Long-term impact
paragraphs: The rebrand turned curious customers into advocates who told their friends. A brand that had started with a mission became one that people didn't just use, they believed in.
